metadata.title: National Collegiate Athletic Assn. v. Smith, 525 U.S. 459 (1999) (No. 98-84)
metadata.creator: Supreme Court of the United States
metadata.description:
Case name: National Collegiate Athletic Assn. v. Smith

Opinion filed: 1999-02-23

Docket No.: 98-84

Citations:
• 142 L. Ed. 2d 929
• 119 S. Ct. 924
• 525 U.S. 459
• 1999 U.S. LEXIS 1511

Case holding summaries:
• "Entities that receive federal assistance, whether directly or through an intermediary, are recipients within the meaning of Title IX; entities that only benefit economically from federal assistance are not."
• regulation defining who is a "recipient" under Title IX
• noting that Title IX, like the Rehabilitation Act, waives immunity only for “[e]ntities that receive federal assistance, whether directly or through an intermediary,” and not for “entities that only benefit economically from federal assistance”
• holding that "entities that only benefit economically from federal assistance are not" recipients
• offering "earmarked" federal funds as one example of such a fact
• receipt of dues from member colleges and universities does not subject NCAA to suit under Title IX
• holding that NCAA was not an indirect recipient of federal funds even though it received dues from schools that received federal funds
• implying that the "controlling authority" theory of Title IX liability has not been addressed by the Supreme Court
• “Entities that receive federal assistance, whether directly or through an intermediary, are recipients within the meaning of Title IX[.]”
• regulation defining who is a “recipient” under Title IX
• "Entities that receive federal assistance, whether directly or through an intermediary, are recipients within the meaning of Title IX; entities that only benefit economically from federal assistance are not."
• holding that the NCAA's acceptance of dues from colleges receiving federal funding did not render the NCAA liable under Title IX
• looking at case law interpreting ง 504 of the Rehabilitation Act to interpret Title IX
• denying NCAA's motion for summary judgment in a Rehabilitation Act suit because "there are genuine questions of material fact as to whether the NCAA receives federal funds through the [National Youth Sports Program Fund]"
• noting that Congress endeavored, in the CRRA, "to correct what it considered to be an unacceptable decision on our part in Grove City "
• receipt of dues from member colleges and universities does not subject NCAA to suit under Title IX
• rejecting suggestion "that the private right of action available under ... § 1681(a) is potentially broader than the Government's enforcement authority"
• relying on Paralyzed Veterans and holding that dues payments from federal funds recipients do not render dues recipient subject to Title IX
